newsitem.title: UK: AEA Technology yr profits up, sees progress.
newsitem.headline: AEA Technology yr profits up, sees progress.

text.p: British science and nuclear technology company AEA Technology Plc said on Monday it saw further progress this year and was looking at possible acquisitions.

The company, formerly part of the state-owned Atomic Energy Authority, said that its first full year results since privatisation last year showed pretax profits of 18.5 million pounds ($30.6 million), up from 15.8 million pounds and it paid out a total dividend of 8.4 pence per share.

The result "reflects the underlying strength of the business in a number of key sectors and we see further opportunities for progress in the coming year," chairman Sir Anthony Cleaver said in a statement.
He added that the company's acquisitions "are progressing and we continue to examine new possibilities."
The company said there had been a decline in business from the UK Atomic Energy Authority but there had been a strong performance in sales to the private sector in Britain and overseas.
AEA Technology said the year had been "an important one in setting down the foundations for sustainable growth."
It said technology costs should be reduced by a restructuring into three main business segments which should also bring "greater cohesiveness to the way customers are serviced."
It added that the nuclear industry would continue to offer opportunities in the UK and overseas, particularly in safety and risk assessment and in plant life extension. ($ = 0.604 British Pounds)
